quest.title: A Knight's Resolve
quest.description: What decision will Lohen make in the face of irrevocable fate? And where will that lead him...?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x650, Primogem x60, Mora x49200, Guide to Resistance x5, Recipe: Mint Bubblegum x1, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hmm... Is this as far as we were able to track him?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Well, he's not known as the 5th Company's "Sharpest Arrow" for nothing. Gone in a flash.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you want to praise him, save it for later! Don't we have any more clues?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: The dew on this grass is cold. Probably the effects of elemental energy.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Oho? You really are something, eh, Honorary Knight?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Still, being spotted by witnesses and leaving traces... That's not the Lohen I know.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Do you think he wants to be followed?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Whether he's in a rush to complete something... or stop something from happening, our task remains the same.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup! Let's get going — we've gotta get to the bottom of this!

choices.text: I should be able to track them.

dialogues.speaker: Cautious Voice
dialogues.text: The experiment results have been confirmed. The serum dosage still requires adjustment...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: These metal scraps and vessels... It's like leading the expedition through Snezhnaya again.

choices.text: The vegetation here is a little strange as well...

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Your earlier conjecture appears correct. This place indeed looks like an experiment site left behind by one of The Doctor's Segments.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: No wonder the Knights of Favonius have failed to discover the entrance for so many years. It was most likely his handiwork.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: And once the concealment faded, someone discovered this place before us, restarting the experiments on Ursa's flesh and blood.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You don't think it was...

response.speaker: Vicious Voice
response.text: What a pain... How many more test subjects do we need to catch...

response.speaker: Vicious Voice
response.text: What are you looking at!?

response.speaker: Vicious Voice
response.text: Stay put, and don't cause any trouble.

choices.text: Could Ursa's power be behind this?

talks.objective: Observe what is happening outside with caution

dialogues.speaker: Respectful Voice
dialogues.text: Sir, the new subjects are here.

dialogues.speaker: Complaining Voice
dialogues.text: This brat's real vicious. Took a lot of work to quiet him down.

dialogues.speaker: Cold Voice
dialogues.text: Hmm? Interesting... I'll take a look myself.

dialogues.speaker: Cold Voice
dialogues.text: Rejoice. You shall soon surpass the common clay of this world. You shall cross into the realm of the extraordinary—

talks.objective: Try to push the door open and leave

dialogues.speaker: Vicious Voice
dialogues.text: I told you. Don't. Cause. Trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Was that... a projection formed using memory?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Seems like a trap laid to slow our advance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A trap? Could it be Lohen again...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Nah. That kid would've come up with something way more... deadly.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: In any case, Lohen isn't the only one...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Who was captured by Eroch and is familiar with this kind of magic.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: ...You don't look like you're here to assist.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: On the contrary, I believe ending this as soon as possible is the best way to help you.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Hmph! Haha... End this? Is that what you're saying now?

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Back when the test subjects were escaping left, right, and center... Back when I was ready to give up... Who was it who said I should keep going?

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Ugh... did all the test subjects... escape?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Uh, you shouldn't experiment on yourself so soon, Theodore.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Did you think that discovering Eroch's lab and taking control of Dottore's apparatus would be enough to help you restart their experiments?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Look at you — you can barely lift a finger, helpless to do anything but watch your test subjects flee.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Lohen... are you... here to stop me?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Heh, quite the opposite. Who do you think kept those monsters from eating you?

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: You... took care of them?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I also plan to deal with the ones that fled into the wild. If you ignore them, the Knights of Favonius will follow them right back to your doorstep.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: You... Why are you helping me?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I know what you intend to do with the flesh and blood of Ursa the Drake. I've read the examination report you wrote for Adorno.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Old and frail, a mass of old injuries... One day, he won't wake up, and no one will be surprised. Without "extraordinary" intervention, that is.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: I... I hid it! Even Adorno himself didn't see it!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Don't be so shocked.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: We're "companions," both rescued by the Benevolent Knight. Did you really think I wouldn't notice your changes?

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: ...Is that why you're willing to keep my secret?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Oh n—no, don't get me wrong. I sincerely hope Adorno can live a while longer — it'd save me from inheriting any unnecessary responsibilities.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: But what I'm more interested in is "power."

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Aren't you concerned that your monster experiments have hit a bottleneck, and that your own body can't bear Ursa's power?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: In that case, use me as your test subject.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Without you, we'd never have come this far!

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Refining the serum, continuing the experiments, bringing Adorno here... Were these ideas not all yours, Lohen?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: That's right. And that's why I'm also prepared for failure.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Failure? We're so... so close. As long as you don't blow our cover, we've still got a shot!

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Lohen, listen to me! The Ursa serum works!

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Adorno's improving. He can get out of bed on his own now! ... If it weren't for you, I don't think he would have lasted the week...

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: But... I can only add low-concentration serum to Adorno's meals and medication for now. It won't cure the root cause...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Is that so? That's good to hear...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: The smoother your experiments go, the greater my hopes of mastering this power.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Uhm... Do you think you could find the time to see him? He talks about you often...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...I—I'll pass. I'd really rather not listen to his nagging.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Besides, unnecessary contact only increases the risk of exposure... We're running out of time.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: The Knights of Favonius will notice something is wrong sooner or later. No matter how many tricks we pull, they'll only work for a time. How much longer until you have complete control?

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Soon! Very soon! Thanks to your help, the serum's power has stabilized substantially, though I wouldn't call it a gentle concoction...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Don't go using it on the old man to save time.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Of course not! You're overthinking this. I know what I'm doing.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Uh-huh. So you say. Everyone assumes they know what they're doing right up until trouble lands on their doorstep.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Haha! If that day ever comes, feel free to slap some sense into me!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Blow our cover? Do you think the Knights never suspected? Who do you think was delaying the investigation?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: How many times do I have to say this? We were gambling from the start — with our time, the Knights' time, and the time Adorno has left...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: If you lose a fight, you retreat. If you lose a bet, you accept it... Linger on the battlefield or at the gambling table, and we're bound to lose even more.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: What do you wanna do, then!? Stand by and watch him die!?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hmph... Wake up already. In his present state, the serum would kill him. Would you prefer that?

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: I haven't given up yet! I... I completed the final refinements before you arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: This is the refined, high-concentration serum... So long as I use this, even you won't be able to stop me!

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: You can refuse to cooperate. That's fine. It just brings me back to where I began. I'll finish this myself!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Relying on hazy childhood memories, Theodore was the first to find this place, restarting Eroch's experiments to prolong Adorno's life.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: But at some point, the experiment failed, and the monsters escaped... Lohen then discovered him and offered his assistance, allowing him to continue extracting serum from Ursa the Drake...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That appears to be the full picture.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: What do you intend to do with them?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: *sigh*... I'll leave that headache to Jean and the others to deal with later. Let them decide the appropriate course to take.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: For now, I'm more concerned about the remains of Ursa's Flesh, buried here beneath the ground...

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Why... I used... the highest... concentration possible!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: You're weak... and you don't even have the self-awareness to realize it.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: ...Self-awareness? What right do you have to talk to me about self-awareness...? You lost control once before as well!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: And that's how I know we can't go on!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: If the price for saving Adorno's life is his very self, then we won't be saving him, but the monster he'll become!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Take a long, hard look in the mirror. Are you really the person he chose to inherit the "Benevolent" name?

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: ...I won't accept this... I can't accept this!

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: ...When was the last time I embraced the two of you like this?

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: In the blink of an eye... you've grown too big for hugs.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: A—Adorno...?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: How did you...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: I heard everything... You've been helping me cling on, haven't you?

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: It's thanks to both of you I have this chance... to hug you once again, just like old times...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: All that's left to say is...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: ...It's alright. It's over now.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Haha. Why the tears? *sigh*... It wouldn't do for the Benevolent Knight to check out by making kids cry now, would it?

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Promise me you'll see me off with a smile.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: I just don't want to... watch you...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Isn't it enough that you're here by my side?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: —Adorno! Theodore!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: —Lohen!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...This issue has been resolved, I take it?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Not entirely.

dialogues.speaker: Low Roar From Deep Within
dialogues.text: Raargh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What... What was that sound!?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I knew it... You had to stimulate Ursa's Flesh beyond the high-risk threshold to extract the necessary serum!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: If its power is allowed to continue overflowing, all nearby lifeforms will be affected... just like the plants here, and those monsters we saw earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: I... Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Why are you still trying to act tough? You can barely lift a finger right now, can you? Huh... I know that feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hand it over, and then... get out of the way and watch.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: ...The key to the underground is in the lining of my coat.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Please... destroy Ursa the Drake's flesh... and its power.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Goodbye... Adorno.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Go. That power was never meant to linger in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Low Roar From Deep Within
dialogues.text: Raargh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Past this point... That's where Eroch and the Doctor conducted their experiments on Ursa, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Sure is. A madman seeking power, and an angel who chose it... What a farce.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...One that we're about to bring the curtain down on.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ursa the Drake's residual power is not to be underestimated. Eyes on the prize, everyone. This'll be a tough fight!

dialogues.speaker: Restless Monsters
dialogues.text: Raargh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa — what was that noise over there!?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Monsters, captured for experiments long ago. They've survived until now thanks to The Doctor's apparatus and Ursa's power.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I added quite a few to their number myself... Looks like they're getting restless.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you really need so many?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you sure your cages are sturdy? We could do without them complicating our fight with Ursa...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: If they were sturdy, I wouldn't have had to work so hard to clean up previous escapees...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: But don't worry, they won't disturb you... I guarantee it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you planning to...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: The ambitions of old subordinates, revenge for beloved family... Those are your grudges to settle, are they not?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: In much the same manner, you just leave the monsters I captured to me.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Oh, one last thing...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius 5th Company — requesting permission to attack.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hah! Finally reporting in before you sortie, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: —Give 'em hell, Lohen.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: And don't die — that's an order.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Haha! In that case, please dispose of Ursa at your earliest convenience.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... Should we help him?

choices.text: No... Let him face this fight alone.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Oho? Looks like that kid's "friendship fee" wasn't a complete waste after all, huh?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: ...Can he handle them all?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Trust him, just as he trusts us. After all, he's set to become the youngest Captain since your appointment.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Eroch, Rerir, Dottore... Hah, and now Ursa? Guess I'm not destined to rise to such challenges.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: But ordinary people... We have our own battles to fight.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: So, go. Settle things with your "obsessions"...

response.speaker: Varka & Lohen
response.text: ...Once and for all!

choices.text: He has his own scores to settle.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: With me! Chaaarge!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Your verdict is...!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Now, begone!

dialogues.speaker: Roar From the Past
dialogues.text: Raargh!

dialogues.speaker: Restless Monsters
dialogues.text: Raargh!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Want to leave, do you? Can you hear Ursa's call? Or is it the serum you smell?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Well, I'm afraid that just won't do. Behind me stand not only heroes who battle wicked dragons, but slow, fragile mortals too.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: So...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Come at me, each and every one of you!

dialogues.speaker: Restless Monsters
dialogues.text: Raargh!

dialogues.speaker: Eroch
dialogues.text: "Rejoice. You shall soon surpass the common clay of this world. You shall cross into the realm of the extraordinary—"
Once, you believed you could control your fate by gaining power.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: "Slow, weak, powerless... mortal."
Then, your paltry arrogance was smashed by power beyond reason.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: "...I accept that we should send our strongest warrior to fight Nod-Krai's battles."
You are not special. That is the truth, one you once thought you had accepted.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: "What do you wanna do, then!? Stand by and watch him die!?"
Yet you will not suffer a mundane death to befall you.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen?
dialogues.text: You are not wrong. You never have been! Power is the sole solution to all things. It is how we grasp destiny by the throat. It is how we resist even Death!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen?
dialogues.text: You simply lack enough of it. Not even close... unless... you accept this gift.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen?
dialogues.text: Power and means are neither good nor evil. Have you not always believed so?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen?
dialogues.text: Carving up Abyssal power, seeking aid from a coven of witches, leaning on divine favor...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen?
dialogues.text: Is there any difference? Are mortals unworthy of power?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen?
dialogues.text: Now then. Accept my strength... <color=#f665ff>My</color> guidance.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Heh, you're right. Power is just power.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...It's humanity's arrogance and stupidity that invite destruction.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen?
dialogues.text: *pained gasp*

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: *panting* Not so talkative now, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen?
dialogues.text: You embrace mediocrity!? You spurn my counsel!?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: What I desire, I'll take with my own two hands. If I accept your guidance, "I" wouldn't be the master of that power now, would I?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Begone. I have no need for power I don't control.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lohen! Wake up! Lohen!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Lohen!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Argh. Are you trying to burst my eardrums? I was just taking a quick nap. That fight took a lot out of me, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Heh. Never thought I'd hear you say something like that.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I didn't inject myself with it. Just used it to attract the monsters. Can't exactly deal with out-of-control monsters when I'm going berserk myself, can I?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Plus, wouldn't want you finishing off Ursa just to turn around and have to deal with me.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: There's still a little in my system from previous experiments, though... That stuff gives you a real headache.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Ursa's Flesh has been destroyed. There shouldn't be any further risk of activation.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...I see. Totally obliterated, huh?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: What about Adorno and Theodore?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Our reinforcements showed up — I had the knights escort them back.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: As for Theodore's punishment... and yours, I'll look into it later.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...Stay with him until the very end, you hear?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Thank you, Grand Master.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: "Do not stand by my grave and cry. My life, I gave to wipe tears dry."

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: "...Here rests the Benevolent Knight..."

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hehe. This epitaph suits you, old man...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who chews bubblegum while visiting a grave...?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh, here to see Adorno too, are you? Hey, want some gum?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uhm, n—no thanks...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: He always liked messing around with this stuff. Said it made the kids happy.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Pretty sure he'd be glad to receive candy on the other side.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I had nothing else to do during confinement, so I made candy to stave off the boredom.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder we didn't see you at the award ceremony... You were in solitary confinement the whole time, huh?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Hah... That wasn't all. Our dear "reasonable" Acting Grand Master Jean handed down two other punishments.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And what were those?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: The Knights have decided to rescind my commendation and not promote me to Captain.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: The title of Benevolent Knight is to be buried with Adorno. The position of 5th Company Captain will also remain vacant — for the time being.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that... really okay!?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: To quote Varka... "Look, Mondstadt did just fine for a long time with only an Acting Grand Master, right?"

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He sure can be persuasive when he wants to be...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: And it's all the more so for the title of Benevolent Knight.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I will not allow anyone unworthy to inherit it... even if the unworthy successor is me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon suddenly felt like that title suited you for a second... Must have been her imagination, eh?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: You think so? I prefer a different title, really. The "Ends Justify the Means Knight"? The "A Win Is a Win Knight"? The "Punching Bag Knight" sounds alright, too.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: That said, it seems this sinner will have to win a few more battles first before getting his next commendation.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Of course. After all, someone once told me.... acknowledging my limits is the first step towards transcending the mundane.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I'll keep winning, no matter what it takes.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Relax. Learning from our mistakes is part and parcel of getting stronger, no? Besides, I know why I pursue power.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Forgetting what you wanted in the first place... That would be true defeat. Do I look like that kind of idiot to you?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Hmm... It's food for thought. Best to have someone on hand to help if something does go wrong.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: In that case, until I'm strong enough to shoulder everything on my own...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Don't grow old on me, alright?

choices.text: But how many people remember in the end?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: According to the experimental logs, extracting high-concentration serum requires repeatedly stimulating Ursa's Flesh to increase its activity...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: There's an ominous feeling growing stronger by the second. Prepare for battle.
